title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
rules: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s containing no repeated characters.
You cannot skip characters. An empty string returns 0.
constraints: 0 <= len(s) <= 50000; letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["abcabcbb"]
Expected: 3

Example 2:
Arguments: ["bbbbb"]
Expected: 1

Example 3:
Arguments: ["pwwkew"]
Expected: 3

title: Minimum Window Substring
rules: Return the shortest contiguous substring of s containing every character of t with the required multiplicity.
If t contains two As, the window must contain at least two As. Character order may differ.
Return an empty string if no window exists. The answer is unique when it exists.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["ADOBECODEBANC","ABC"]
Expected: "BANC"

Example 2:
Arguments: ["a","a"]
Expected: "a"

Example 3:
Arguments: ["a","aa"]
Expected: ""

title: Regular Expression Matching
rules: Return whether pattern p matches the entire string s. A partial match returns False.
. matches any single character; * repeats the preceding element zero or more times.
For example, a* matches the empty string, a, aa, and so on. The pattern is valid.
constraints: 1 <= len(s), len(p) <= 20; s: lowercase letters; p: lowercase letters, '.' and '*'.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["aa","a"]
Expected: false

Example 2:
Arguments: ["aa","a*"]
Expected: true

Example 3:
Arguments: ["ab",".*"]
Expected: true

title: Edit Distance
rules: Return the minimum number of operations needed to transform word1 into word2.
An operation inserts, deletes, or replaces one character. Keeping an identical character costs nothing.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["horse","ros"]
Expected: 3

Example 2:
Arguments: ["intention","execution"]
Expected: 5

title: String to Integer (atoi)
rules: Skip leading spaces (' '), then read one optional + or - sign.
Read consecutive digits and stop at the first nondigit. Return 0 if no digits are read.
Clamp the result to the signed 32-bit integer range [-2147483648, 2147483647].
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["42"]
Expected: 42

Example 2:
Arguments: ["   -042"]
Expected: -42

Example 3:
Arguments: ["1337c0d3"]
Expected: 1337

title: Group Anagrams
rules: Group words that can be made identical by rearranging their characters.
Preserve all input words, including duplicates. Group order and order within each group are unrestricted.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: [["eat","tea","tan","ate","nat","bat"]]
Expected: [["bat"],["nat","tan"],["ate","eat","tea"]]

Example 2:
Arguments: [[""]]
Expected: [[""]]

Example 3:
Arguments: [["a"]]
Expected: [["a"]]

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
rules: Return the longest contiguous substring of s that reads the same forwards and backwards.
Return the string itself, not its length. Any longest answer is acceptable if several exist.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["babad"]
Expected: "bab"

Example 2:
Arguments: ["cbbd"]
Expected: "bb"

title: ZigZag Conversion
rules: Arrange the string in numRows rows, moving downwards and then diagonally upwards in a zigzag.
Return the characters of each row from left to right, concatenated from top row to bottom.
If numRows is 1, return the original string unchanged.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["PAYPALISHIRING",3]
Expected: "PAHNAPLSIIGYIR"

Example 2:
Arguments: ["PAYPALISHIRING",4]
Expected: "PINALSIGYAHRPI"

Example 3:
Arguments: ["A",1]
Expected: "A"

title: Valid Parentheses
rules: Return whether a string containing only (), {}, and [] is correctly balanced.
Each opening bracket must close with the same type, and the most recently opened bracket must close first.
Every bracket must be paired.
examples:
Example 1:
Arguments: ["()"]
Expected: true

Example 2:
Arguments: ["()[]{}"]
Expected: true

Example 3:
Arguments: ["(]"]
Expected: false

title: String Compression
rules: Compress consecutive groups of identical characters in chars in place at the start of the same array.
For a group of length 1, write only the character. For length 2 or more, append each digit of the count separately.
Return the compressed length k as an integer. chars[:k] is also checked; the remaining contents are ignored. Use O(1) extra space.
Example: aabcccccaaa → a2bc5a3. Unlike b1 in the post, LeetCode 443 omits counts of 1.
constraints: 1 <= len(chars) <= 2000; each element is one letter, digit or symbol.
